title: After the scribe: where health AI goes next
desc: The AI scribe was the easy win. The real 2026 question is what AI does after the note: in the back office where the money and the misery live.

title: The agentic solo operator: a team of one
desc: Agentic AI removed the ceiling on what one operator can ship. Field notes from running a full growth engine solo: where judgment, not labor, is the limit.

title: Aging happens fast now: before the systems are ready
desc: Bangladesh's over-60s nearly double by 2050 with no home-care model; the US market tops $250B. Elder care is the next market almost nobody's building yet.

title: AI Is Now Beating Human Drug Discovery on Its Own Numbers
desc: 200+ AI-designed drugs are in clinical development with 80-90% Phase I success versus 40-65% traditionally. AI isn't just faster at discovery, it's more accurate.

title: AI can translate words, not localize culture
desc: AI dubbing cuts localization cost 70-90%; translation is nearly free. But translating words isn't localizing culture: and that gap is where judgment wins.

title: AI Closes the Diagnosis Gap Bangladesh Can't Wait For
desc: Bangladesh has 170M people and a specialist shortage no pipeline closes fast enough. AI triage isn't a supplement there, it's the first clinician many meet.

title: 86 New AI Medical Devices in One Quarter Is a Maturity Story
desc: Q2 2026: 86 new FDA-cleared AI/ML medical devices, spreading beyond radiology into cardiology, dental, and pathology. This is regulatory maturity, not hype.

title: Verification Is the Real Product of Running AI in Production
desc: The gap between an AI demo and a production system is verification architecture. Inside the source-checking and refusal design that keeps 155 sessions fact-clean.

title: AI for the two-person Dhaka business
desc: Everyone tells the enterprise AI story. The one that matters: a two-person Dhaka shop running like a twenty-person one: an SME's first affordable team.

title: AI's Real Bottleneck Isn't the Model, It's the Grid
desc: Data center electricity demand grows 26% in 2026 to 565 TWh, with AI servers drawing 31% of it. Power, not model quality, is now deciding who wins the AI race.

title: AI Now Vets Your Employer Brand Before a Candidate Does
desc: AI traffic to careers pages surged 1,300% in six months, and 38% of jobseekers under 30 ask AI directly which employers fit them. Employer brand needs GEO now.

title: Air quality is a health emergency nobody owns
desc: Dhaka's air ranks among the world's worst: PM2.5 ~13x the WHO limit: and US wildfire smoke made the threat American. High-leverage, and no one owns it.

title: The slow pandemic: antimicrobial resistance
desc: Antimicrobial resistance may kill 39 million by 2050: three a minute, South Asia hardest hit. A behavior and communication problem, and so it's neglected.

title: The authenticity dividend - your last real moat
desc: In a feed drowning in AI sameness, the scarce thing is proof a person made it. Notes on trust: from Dhaka's markets to the backlash against AI slop.

title: Bangla-first AI: the market the giants keep skipping
desc: Bengali is a top-seven world language yet barely a fraction of the web. A builder's dual-market case for the Bangla-first AI opportunity the giants overlook.

title: The pendulum swings back to brand
desc: Performance marketers report diminishing returns, ad spend passed $1T, and AI floods every channel with sameness. The scarce asset: a brand people trust.

title: Building in public with AI: what I learned running my own
desc: I didn't just write about AI this quarter: I ran it. A system built for my own work: 155 sessions, zero fabricated facts, verification built in from the start.

title: I rebuilt my website to be read by AI, not just Google
desc: 80% of searches now end without a click. Field notes on optimizing for answer engines: structured data, llms.txt, and becoming the source AI actually cites.

title: How mental health became the premium category
desc: Investors once treated mental health as charity. In 2026 a mental-health app sold for $865M. The demand was always there: someone designed around the barrier.

title: 507 Million Children by 2040: A Capacity Problem, Not a Willpower One
desc: World Obesity Atlas 2026: 507 million children overweight or obese by 2040. China, India, and South Asia lead the scale. Health systems need a 15-year plan now.

title: Clarity is an intervention, not polish
desc: We treat clarity as polish. It isn't. Confusing health guidance has a body count and a price tag: clarity is itself a health intervention.

title: Clean hands, still: the cheapest health tech we underuse
desc: Bangladesh hit 98% water access, yet arsenic poisons ~50M; the US is still pulling 9M lead pipes. Water and hygiene: the highest-return health tech, underused.

title: The cold chain is the product, not the pill
desc: US drug shortages hit 223 in early 2026, lasting five-plus years. For medicines, logistics is the health outcome: and whoever owns the last cold inch wins.

title: Companion Bots Just Got Regulated Like a Health Product
desc: California's SB 243 and a parallel New York law now require AI companion apps to disclose, detect self-harm risk, and protect minors, after 72% of teens used one.

title: Losing One Nurse Costs a Hospital $60,090
desc: US hospitals lose $60,090 every time an RN leaves, $5.19M a year on average. Why retention is a P&L problem, not an HR one.

title: Create the category, don't compete in one
desc: Positioning wins a slot someone else defined. The stronger move: design the category itself: name the problem, set the terms, become the default answer.

title: The Creator Economy's Math Problem
desc: 207 million people call themselves creators in a $248.95B market, but only 4% earn over $100K a year. The gap between reach and revenue, and why it matters.

title: CSAT Over Revenue
desc: 55% of CMOs now name customer satisfaction, not revenue growth, as their primary success metric, up from 42% in 2023. What that quiet shift actually means.

title: Telehealth's Fourth Extension Shows Regulatory Uncertainty Is a Distribution Problem
desc: DEA and HHS extended telemedicine prescribing through 2026, a fourth temporary fix, still no permanent rule. Uncertainty is itself a distribution problem.

title: The mosquito economy: dengue is a climate problem now
desc: Bangladesh logged 102,000+ dengue cases last year; 2026 is climbing. It's no longer only ours: local dengue is turning up in the US. Climate rewrote the map.

title: The lab is the wedge: diagnostics-led care
desc: In cash-pay markets the cheapest way into care isn't a doctor: it's a test. I built care that led with the lab, the model richer markets rediscover at home.

title: The middle is disappearing: digital health's $4B quarter
desc: Digital health raised $4B last quarter and 12 companies took 59%. What that concentration and "AI as table stakes" mean for everyone who isn't a megadeal.

title: The dual-market operator's edge
desc: Most operators compete in one market. I read two: the US and Bangladesh: daily. Sixteen years taught me that bridge is a position no one else can occupy.

title: The DRC's Ebola Outbreak Is a Trust Problem, Not a Virology One
desc: 1,406 Ebola cases in the DRC, and WHO cites community mistrust and violence as the active blocker, not the virus. Outbreak response is a trust problem first.

title: The EU AI Act's Enforcement Deadline Is a Redesign Brief
desc: Full enforcement of the EU AI Act begins August 2, 2026, with fines up to €35M or 7% of global turnover. Compliance is a redesign problem, not a legal one.

title: Everyone says "AI-powered" - position on the job
desc: When every booth claims the same edge, the phrase means nothing. Positioning must move where copycats can't follow: the job the customer is hiring you to do.

title: FemTech's £1.5M Government Check Is an Anchor, Not Just Funding
desc: The UK launched a £1.5M FemTech fund under its Women's Health Strategy, public money now formally backing a category private demand alone couldn't scale.

title: Femtech: health's clearest open market
desc: Women's health is worth tens of billions, yet barely 4% of biopharma R&D addressed it. The under-served half of the population is health's clearest open market.

title: Financing the uninsured: the missing rail in health
desc: In Bangladesh, out-of-pocket costs are ~68.5% of health spending; ~70M face hardship. The fix isn't a clinic: it's a payment rail I built at national scale.

title: The First Fully AI-Designed Drug Could Get FDA Approval Within the Year
desc: Insilico's rentosertib is the first fully AI-designed drug in Phase IIb, with a 60% shot at approval by 2027. Why verification, not design, is the real bottleneck.

title: Frugal innovation as a design philosophy
desc: The West calls it "frugal innovation." In Bangladesh we called it getting it done. The design principles of 2026 are what scarcity taught us years ago.

title: The Gen Z Pay Cut for Ethics
desc: 86% of Gen Z say workplace purpose shapes their happiness, and roughly two-thirds would take a lower salary for an ethical employer. Why employer brand is now a P&L lever.

title: GLP-1s: the drug was never the hard part
desc: Only ~12% of Americans take a GLP-1, and most who start quit. Pharma solved the biology; behavior and adherence decide the outcome: the layer I've built on.

title: Where Did the Graduate Jobs Go
desc: Entry-level graduate roles fell 33% year-on-year, 17,000 openings for 1.2M applicants. What the collapse means for employer brand, from the UK to Bangladesh.

title: Where health AI actually lands by 2027: a builder's bet
desc: Adoption is done. Three bets on where health AI actually lands by 2027: people over models, judgment, and plumbing: each grounded in work I've shipped.

title: Health communication that changes behavior
desc: Information isn't the same as behavior. Field lessons on segmentation, friction, framing, and measurement, from population-scale and campus health campaigns.

title: The healthtech leapfrog Bangladesh already made
desc: Bangladesh jumped from cash straight to mobile money. In health tech the same leapfrog is the opening: build access-first, not a copy of the US. I've run it.

title: Heat Kills on Moderate Days, Not Extreme Ones
desc: NYC data: 80% of heat deaths happen on moderately hot days, not extreme ones. The highest-impact public health message is rarely the dramatic headline.

title: A hotline on a bar of soap - distribution wins
desc: The best health channel I ever used wasn't an app or an ad: it was a bar of soap. Putting a clinic inside a product people owned took ~3,000 calls a day.

title: LinkedIn's Algorithm Reads Your Bio Before It Reads Your Post
desc: LinkedIn's 2026 algorithm reads your headline and About for topical authority before deciding a post's reach. Credibility is set before you hit publish.

title: Saves, Not Likes: What 300,000 LinkedIn Posts Actually Show
desc: LinkedIn's 2026 analysis of 300,000 posts: saves beat likes as the top ranking signal, polls are bad for growth, and hashtags haven't worked in years.

title: Loneliness Is Worse in Poor Countries, Not Rich Ones
desc: WHO's Commission on Social Connection found loneliness hits low-income countries hardest, 24% versus 11%. The fix isn't a clinic. It's an accessible channel.

title: Measles is back: a trust problem, not a supply problem
desc: The US passed 2,200 measles cases in 2026: a trust problem, not supply. Why messengers beat facts, from a soap-packet hotline in Dhaka to a US campus campaign.

title: Measure the number you're avoiding
desc: Every team measures something. The winning ones measure the number they'd rather not look at: and decide what to count before they start, not after.

title: Medical Debt's Racial Gap Is a Margin Question in Disguise
desc: 56% of Black adults carry medical debt versus 37% of White adults. Bangladesh's out-of-pocket burden resolves the same question differently, who absorbs the cost.

title: The nutrition transition: the environment is the disease
desc: Bangladesh now carries undernutrition and diabetes at once; the US drowns in the same processed calories. The food environment, not willpower, is the disease.

title: The personal-brand playbook for the markets everyone ignores
desc: The most underrated growth asset in 2026 isn't a company brand: it's a person's. And the biggest opening to build one is where Western creators aren't looking.

title: The pharmacy is the front door of care
desc: In Bangladesh care begins at the pharmacist; in the US ~50M live in a pharmacy desert. Same underused node: the pharmacy as health's real front door.

title: The US Could Be Short 86,000 Doctors by 2036
desc: AAMC projects the US could be 86,000 physicians short by 2036, but the real gap, at full care parity, is 202,800. Here's what that means.

title: Prevention-first: the design window that closes
desc: The US didn't choose sick-care: it backed into what the money rewarded. A market still building its system has an option the US lost: put prevention first.

title: Pricing is positioning, not a spreadsheet
desc: Your price is the loudest thing your brand says. In cash markets where every taka is felt, pricing is your sharpest positioning decision: not a spreadsheet.

title: Provenance over volume - AI's next health win
desc: The AI health rush chases the wrong verb. Everyone races to generate more; the scarce thing was never volume: it's proving what's true and where it came from.

title: The remittance-to-health pipeline
desc: Bangladesh took in a record $35.56B in remittances while ~70M face health hardship. Connect them: the country's biggest untapped health-financing rail.

title: Retail Media Hits $203.9B While 76% of Purchases Still Happen In Store
desc: Retail media is projected to hit $203.9B in 2026, up 14%, yet 76% of purchases still happen in stores. Digital-first hype meets where buying happens.

title: Retention is the real growth engine
desc: Acquisition costs rose ~60% in five years. Winners obsess over the leaky bucket: cash markets taught me retention, not reach, is the growth engine.

title: Roads are a health crisis we refuse to own
desc: Bangladesh had its deadliest road year in 2025: 9,000+ lives: while the US cut its toll. Same machine, opposite paths: one treats road death as designable.

title: Rural America Is Running Out of Places to Give Birth
desc: 139 rural US hospitals have cut labor and delivery since 2020, a 13% drop in rural birth capacity. Here's the distribution fix hospitals aren't trying yet.

title: Shame is a design flaw: not a personal failing
desc: Shame feels like clarity but works like a wall. In health comms, stigma is a barrier you design around: channel, framing, segmentation: not lecture away.

title: Commerce runs on chat, not storefronts
desc: Bangladesh runs one of the world's largest F-commerce ecosystems: 300,000+ sellers working from a chat thread. People buy from a person, not a store.

title: Stop throwing away what you publish
desc: The most wasteful thing in content isn't a bad idea: it's a good one you published once and dropped. Atomize a few durable assets instead of churning posts.

title: Telehealth's second act: care that comes to you
desc: Telehealth's first act was pandemic video for the waiting room. The second act is less a video call and more care delivered to your home, on your schedule.

title: The call-center cliff and AI voice agents
desc: AI voice agents are coming for the call-center economy: Bangladesh built ~$850M and 85,000 jobs on it. Can we move people up the value chain fast enough?

title: The consent problem - health AI's real bottleneck
desc: Every debate about health AI fixates on accuracy. What actually stalls it is trust by design: consent, privacy, and provenance: the layer nobody demos.

title: The first 1,000 days: the highest-ROI window in health
desc: Bangladesh cut maternal deaths 79%; the US is the only developed country where they rise. Conception to age two is where a health dollar does the most work.

title: The last mile - health tech's untapped value
desc: Most health tech serves the first mile: the hospital. The untapped value is the last mile: the person far from care, reached where they are.

title: The model's blind spot is your opportunity
desc: AI models learn from a lopsided web. Every language and market it underrepresents is where models are weak: and where you can win. The gap is the opening.

title: GLP-1 Spawned a Whole Services Economy: Separate From the Drug Itself
desc: Three $100M+ raises hit GLP-1 services in H1 2026. The opportunity isn't the drug, it's the economy forming around it, from the US to Bangladesh.

title: The quiet epidemic: tobacco and the new nicotine
desc: Tobacco kills ~158,000 a year in Bangladesh: one in five deaths; the US fight moved to youth vaping. Same economy, opposite framing: shaming never wins it.

title: The Shrinking CMO
desc: Marketing budgets are flat at 7.7% of revenue, 95% of CMOs feel ROI pressure, and tenure hit a 10-year low of 4.1 years. What keeps a growth leader standing.

title: The trust cold-start in two-sided health platforms
desc: Every platform faces the same first problem: nobody comes because nobody's there. In health it's worse: the currency isn't supply and demand, it's trust.

title: The Verification Gap in AI Code
desc: 96% of developers don't fully trust AI-generated code, only 48% verify it every time. The risk was never bad code, it's shipping with no verification layer.

title: Trust in the pill: the counterfeit-medicine problem
desc: One in ten medicines in poorer countries is substandard or fake: a trust collapse you engineer out of the supply. Rich-world shortages open the same door.

title: When nobody trusts anybody, trust is the growth strategy
desc: In low-trust categories, trust isn't a brand value: it's the growth engine. From moving 10 million onto digital payments where trust was the entire barrier.

title: The $200M question: where to spend it on health
desc: The World Bank put $200M into Bangladesh's primary care. Given real money, where does a health dollar actually change an outcome? My answer isn't a shiny app.

title: Voice-first AI for the next billion
desc: The last billion online won't type: they'll talk. Voice skips the two barriers keeping AI from those who need it most: literacy and the keyboard.

title: When patients pay cash, everything about the product changes
desc: In the US, health products are built for a payer. In most of the world the patient pays: and that fact is a design discipline the US is drifting toward.

title: When the buyer is an AI, not a person
desc: Google's "Buy for me" and ChatGPT Shopping mean the next shopper is an agent, not a person. Agentic commerce may hit $3-5T: few brands are built for it.

title: The workforce crisis and the community-health-worker answer
desc: America's health system is short of people, not technology. The answer is a model Bangladesh has run for decades: move tasks to those closest to the community.

title: Zero Digital Health IPOs in Six Months: the Exit Bar Just Changed
desc: Zero digital health IPOs landed in H1 2026. Hinge Health's stock doubled anyway, because it cleared the Rule of 40. Here's what changed.
